request.acceptance_criteria: Frame tests (terminal-emulator screen grid) assert the colour attribute per state: a closed group is dim, an in-flight pipeline stage amber, a failed/held row red, needs-you red+bold when non-empty, ids cyan; NO_COLOR renders no SGR colour codes with an identical layout; screenshots of the dashboard at 120x40 and 80x24 attached to the report per the 'work someone will see' pattern. make gate passes.
request.description: Operator, 2026-10-05, after reviewing screenshots of the dashboard at 120x40 and 80x24 (nearly monochrome; only 'healthy' is green): use DISCRETE colour accents — colour carries meaning, sparingly, never decoration. Semantic palette (ANSI 16-colour names so terminal themes map them; no background fills except the progress bar): green = done/closed/passed/healthy; amber/yellow = in flight/working/stall warning; red = failed/rejected/held/needs-you (the needs-you line is the most prominent thing on screen when non-empty); cyan = tick ids and key hints; dim/grey = secondary text (closed groups, provenance like 'glm-5.3 · herdr', the feed tail's timestamps, 'not metered'); bold for section headers (TICK…, WORKERS, recent). At most these four hues. Respect NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb (plain text, same layout); colour never changes widths. Apply the same palette to the drill-in and feed views; the plain-lines mode stays uncoloured when stdout is not a terminal.
request.title: watch dashboard uses discrete colour accents
